The combination of leafy/herbal notes (classic cool-climate Cab Franc pyrazine character), olive and cherry, plus the acknowledgment of underripeness from a cool vintage, points most strongly to Cabernet Franc — this profile (savory olive-cherry with a green, leafy edge and elegant structure) is a textbook descriptor for it, especially from a cooler year like 2010. Sangiovese shares the olive/cherry/savory signature (think Chianti) but is less associated with the "leafy herb/underripe" note. Merlot can show similar herbal-cherry traits in a cool year but typically reads plusher rather than "elegant and fresh."
